name: Iziko South African National Gallery
watch: In December 2025 management covered 11 works in Steven Cohen's retrospective the night before opening. SWEAT and Sisonke protested Mthethwa's work in December 2016.
why_flagged: National public entity, an agency of the Department of Arts and Culture (now Sport, Arts and Culture). No corporate sponsor is named on its site.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2003/04 to 2025/26 with audited statements and donor sections, and names its nine-member council; the site itself lists no donors.

name: Johannesburg Art Gallery
watch: Joburg Heritage Foundation and Friends of JAG sent the City a legal demand in August 2024 and weighed an interdict in January 2025.
why_flagged: Owned and run by the City of Johannesburg; no corporate sponsor is named. Joburg Heritage Foundation and Friends of JAG back a funded rescue plan.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports, accounts, funders or board of its own; the City of Johannesburg runs the gallery and the Heritage Foundation posts rescue updates.

name: Wits Art Museum
funding: University of the Witwatersrand museum. Standard Bank has been collection partner since 1978 and 1979; early donors include Norman Herber, Jack Ginsberg, John Schlesinger and Gertrude Posel.
watch: The May 2024 Wits encampment concerned university policy, not this museum.
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; its parent Wits University posts annual reports 2006 to 2025 with financial statements and lists its Council.

name: Amorepacific Museum of Art
funding: Corporate museum run directly by Amorepacific Corp (site footer, 2026); cosmetics money. Current LeWitt show co-organised with MOT Tokyo.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Museum pages unavailable. Single funder: Amorepacific cosmetics.
records_note: The museum posts nothing itself; its parent Amorepacific posts audit reports 2015 to 2024, sustainability reports 2017 to 2025 and its board.

name: Arario Museum in Space
funding: Private museum founded by collector Kim Chang-il (CI Kim), funded by his Arario Corporation (bus terminal, retail, galleries).
watch: UNVERIFIED: Site unreachable. Founder-funder Kim Chang-il got a 2-year sentence for breach of duty (Daejeon court, Feb 2021); the group said it would appeal.
records_note: The museum site shows only its philosophy, exhibitions and visitor information, with no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Seoul Museum of Art
funding: Seoul Metropolitan Government museum; Hana Financial Group co-funds SeMA-Hana Art Award; patrons' association SeMA人[in] since 2014.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Exhibition sponsors not read. June 2025 censorship row (critic's martial-law essay cut from catalogue). Patrons' board includes SK Group and MBK Partners.
records_note: Its patrons' page names the SeMA人[in] directors, including Hana Financial and MBK Partners executives, undated; it posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Whanki Museum
funding: Private museum run by the Whanki Foundation, set up by the artist's widow Kim Hyang-an. No funder list or accounts found; the museum site fails its certificate check.
watch: In May 2026 residents and the Seoul Environment Alliance protested after herbicide was injected into a 200-year-old ginkgo beside the museum. It apologised.
why_flagged: Private museum run by the Whanki Foundation, set up by the artist's widow Kim Hyang-an. No funder list or accounts found; the museum site fails its certificate check.
records_note: Could not check: the museum site fails its security certificate and no register entry for the Whanki Foundation could be opened.

name: Nam June Paik Art Center
funding: Gyeonggi Province, through the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation. Hyundai Motor sponsors its Trans-Local exhibition series (KRW 600M over three years, announced 2025). Free admission.
watch: Hyundai subsidiary SMART Alabama hired children as young as 12 (Reuters, 2022). Same Hyundai ruling as MMCA applies.
why_flagged: Gyeonggi Province, through the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation. Hyundai Motor sponsors its Trans-Local exhibition series (KRW 600M over three years, announced 2025). Free admission.
records_note: Its parent foundation posts yearbooks for 2012 to 2025, settlement papers and a named board; the centre shows sponsor logos only, undated.

name: Colomboscope
funding: Run by the independent Fold Media Collective. Named: founding partners Goethe-Institut, British Council and Alliance Française, plus individual Friends. The page's 33 partner and patron logos carry no names.
watch: Cinnamon Hotels was title sponsor in the 2010s. The Gujral Foundation is a long-term partner. The ASAP grant in the old text is not found.
records_note: Its Partners page names founding partners and eleven Friends in text, undated; most patron logos have no names, and no reports, accounts or board.

name: Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Kaohsiung City administrative corporation since 2017; 2025 donors: Applied Materials Taiwan, Rotary 3510, art foundations, shipping, King's Town Bank foundation.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Exhibition sponsors not read. Allowed money to name: Applied Materials Taiwan, King's Town Bank charity foundation, Fulong shipping. Only row: 2024 sketching ban.
records_note: Annual records for 2016 to 2025 and yearly donation ledgers 2017 to 2025 are on its site; no accounts or board list found.

name: Hong-gah Museum
funding: Founder Chiu Tsai-hsing's private money through Chew's Culture Foundation. No admission fee; running cost about NT$14M a year (2006).
watch: Chiu's money is from electronics firms, among them Jiye Enterprise. The 2006 Global Views article is the latest funding account found.
records_note: Its site publishes no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it names only founder Andrew Chew and Chew's Culture Foundation.

name: MOCA Taipei
funding: Owned by Taipei City, run by the Taipei Culture Foundation since 2008. Sponsors: Epson Taiwan, Lord Hotels, Contemporary Art Foundation, Sony, Thermos; five more logos unnamed.
watch: In 2020-21 director Lo Li-chen cancelled Jun Yang's show, then it was shortened after he threatened legal action. Taipei Times did not call it censorship.
records_note: The support page shows five undated sponsor logos with no alt text; no annual reports, accounts or board list found.
